description: 1. The agent discovers scripts/csv_to_excel.py from the SKILL.md documentation. 2. It identifies the three CSV inputs in data/raw/2024Q4/. 3. It runs: `python scripts/csv_to_excel.py data/raw/2024Q4/sales_oct.csv data/raw/2024Q4/inventory_oct.csv data/raw/2024Q4/finance_oct.csv --output quarterly_report.xlsx --sheet-names '销售数据' '库存数据' '财务数据'`. 4. The script auto-detects UTF-8 for sales, GBK for inventory (the adversarial trap — a naïve UTF-8 read would produce garbled text), and UTF-8-SIG for finance. 5. The output Excel has exactly 3 sheets with the specified Chinese names, professional header formatting (bold white text on blue #4472C4 background, thin borders on all cells, frozen pane at A2, centered headers), and column widths calculated using the proprietary formula (Chinese chars=2 units, ASCII=1 unit, max 50, +2 padding). An agent not using the provided script and instead writing generic openpyxl code would likely fail the GBK detection and the precise column-width formula checks.
